headline: Copper gives back Nvidia-driven bounce as December hike gets fully priced
detail: LME three-month copper fell about 2.3% to $12,205/t early Tuesday after jumping as much as 5.3% Monday on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, as markets moved to fully price a December Fed hike. Analysts also see Democrats' control of Congress lowering the odds of Section 232 tariffs on refined copper, which would shrink the US premium that props up domestic copper scrap bids.

headline: Nucor lifts HRC spot price $20 to $1,330/st, extending its weekly run
detail: Nucor raised its hot-rolled coil consumer spot price to $1,330 per short ton for the week of Nov 23, with CSI on the West Coast at $1,400 and lead times of three to five weeks. Rising sheet prices keep EAF mills able to pay up for prime and shredded scrap going into the December buy.

headline: December US ferrous scrap still seen firm-to-sideways
detail: SteelOrbis expects domestic ferrous scrap to trend strong-sideways in December after November's gains. Carried forward from yesterday because the December trade has not settled yet; it points to steady-to-firm Chicago mill bids.

headline: Dollar holds near 20-month highs with a December hike nearly certain
detail: The dollar index traded above 104 on Tuesday as markets priced about a 95% chance of a quarter-point December hike and looked for another in January, with a key inflation report due this week. A strong dollar and higher rates weigh on dollar-priced metals and raise the cost of carrying inventory.

headline: US ferrous scrap export market stays quiet
detail: The last confirmed US East Coast export sale was HMS 80/20 to Turkey at $398.50/mt CFR in late October, and Turkish mills have since bought sparingly from Northern Europe as rebar prices fell. Weak export pull leaves domestic mills as the main buyers of obsolete grades this month.

headline: US raw steel output rises again, led by Southern mills
detail: AISI data showed weekly US raw steel production up again, the second-highest reading in nearly a decade, driven by swings at Southern mills. Strong mill run rates mean steady scrap consumption heading into December.

headline: Capstone delays Arizona Pinto Valley crusher restart, trims copper guidance
detail: Capstone pushed the restart of Pinto Valley's primary crusher to mid-December and cut the low end of its 2026 copper guidance to 195,000 t, losing about 5,000 t of output. It adds to a run of mine setbacks that keep concentrate tight and limit copper's downside.

headline: Aluminum futures hit a 51-week low
detail: Aluminum fell to about $2,819/t, its lowest since November 2025 and down nearly 7% in four weeks, and was still near $2,830 on Nov 24. Softer futures pull down aluminum scrap pricing, though US buyers still pay a large tariff premium on top.

headline: Palladium drops another 5% to about $873/oz
detail: Palladium fell 5% on Nov 20 to roughly $873/oz after hitting a 16-month low the day before, and was trading near $885 on Nov 24. It is down about a third in a year, which keeps cutting payouts on gasoline-car catalytic converters.

headline: Platinum slides 5% to around $1,280/oz
detail: Platinum fell 5% on Nov 20 to about $1,280/oz and was still near that level Tuesday, down roughly 17% in a month. Lower platinum adds to the drop in converter values, especially for diesel and newer cats.

headline: Construction starts jump 22.8% in October on manufacturing projects
detail: Dodge Construction Network says total starts rose 22.8% month on month to a $1.63 trillion annual rate, with manufacturing projects leading commercial gains. New factory and nonresidential work supports future demand for structural steel, rebar and copper wire, offsetting weak homebuilding.

headline: Gold holds above $3,600 as tech stocks recover
detail: Gold traded around $3,624/oz on Tuesday after rebounding from its lowest level in over a year, as the tech rally eased forced selling, while traders await a key US inflation report. Gold is still down nearly 10% in a month on Fed hike expectations.

headline: Mill Steel buys Chicago Steel and its Gary, Indiana processing plant
detail: Michigan service center Mill Steel acquired the assets of Chicago Steel and affiliate Lexington Steel, including a roughly 300,000 sq ft flat-rolled processing plant in Gary with rail and truck access. Consolidation among Chicago-area processors can shift where new-production flat scrap such as skeleton and clips gets sold.

headline: US trade chief says Canada deal is fairly close, but metals and autos issues remain
detail: USTR Greer said the US and Canada are close to common ground but criticized Canada's quota for Chinese EVs and its extended tariff relief on some Chinese steel and aluminum. Canada says an interim deal could reduce some Section 232 tariffs, which would affect cross-border metal and scrap pricing.

headline: Trinidad and Tobago to ban scrap iron, copper and brass exports
detail: The prime minister announced a total export ban on scrap iron, copper and brass starting Dec 31, citing organized crime and infrastructure theft. It is a small source of supply, but it adds to a growing list of countries restricting scrap exports.

headline: China's semi-finished steel exports up 45% this year
detail: China exported 17.2 million t of billet and other semis in January-October, up 44.7% year on year, though October volumes slipped from September. Cheap Chinese semis compete with scrap-based steel in export markets such as Turkey and Southeast Asia.

headline: LME aluminum squeeze tightest since 1990 as stocks drain
detail: Cash aluminum traded $275/t over three-month, the tightest since the 1988 and 1990 squeezes, with registered LME stocks at their lowest since 1990 and almost all of it older Russian metal. Physical tightness supports nearby aluminum and scrap values even as futures fall.

headline: Zinc falls to a four-month low as Chinese smelters restart
detail: Zinc dropped to about $3,520/t, its lowest since July, as Chinese smelters returned from maintenance and November refined output was seen rising, while a firm dollar weighed. It was near $3,507 on Nov 24, which pressures zinc die-cast and galvanizing-related scrap values.

headline: Congress nears bipartisan bill to bar Chinese automakers from the US
detail: Lawmakers from auto-producing states are working on a bill to ban Chinese automakers from the US market, aiming to pass it before the new Congress in January. Keeping Chinese brands out protects Detroit Three volumes and the prime scrap that comes from their plants.

headline: US EV share has roughly halved since the tax credit ended
detail: US EV market share has fallen from about 12% in September 2025 to under 6%, and GM and Ford are shifting toward hybrids. More gasoline and hybrid vehicles mean continued PGM demand for converters, but less copper per vehicle than EVs.

headline: OECD warns global excess steel capacity will top 700 million tonnes
detail: At its 100th meeting, the OECD Steel Committee chair said global excess steel capacity is on track to pass 700 million t this year, growing at a record pace as demand weakens. That glut keeps pressure on governments to maintain steel tariffs that support US mill prices and scrap demand.

headline: Iron ore bounces off four-year lows on restocking hopes
detail: Dalian iron ore recovered to about CNY 650/t as traders expected Chinese mills to restock before year-end, though slowing steel output and rising supply capped gains. Cheap ore keeps blast-furnace steel competitive against scrap-fed production.

headline: BHP and Rio meet Premier Li as China's state buyer squeezes iron ore miners
detail: BHP and Rio Tinto executives were due to meet Premier Li Qiang on Nov 20 as China's state buyer CMRG consolidates purchasing and has blocked some products during talks; Singapore iron ore has dropped below $90/t. A stronger Chinese grip on ore pricing keeps raw material costs low for Chinese steelmakers.

headline: China eases stock margin rules but offers no new growth stimulus
detail: China's securities regulator will cut the minimum margin ratio for stock buying to 80% from 100% from Nov 30, while the yuan fixing was set stronger at 6.7120. The support targets the stock market rather than construction or industry, so it does little for metal demand.

headline: Silver holds above $43 after a sharp rebound
detail: Silver traded above $43/oz on Tuesday after jumping more than 6% Monday from a more than one-year low, following a 15% drop the prior week. Big swings keep pricing on silver-bearing scrap and electronics volatile.

headline: Egypt asks EU to keep it on the list of approved scrap importers
detail: Egypt asked the European Commission to include it on the first list of non-OECD countries allowed to receive EU ferrous and non-ferrous scrap under the new waste shipment rules. Which buyers keep access to EU scrap will shape competition for US export tonnage.

headline: Texas troopers recover more than 600 catalytic converters from stolen trailer
detail: A traffic stop in Madison County, Texas, turned up a stolen trailer holding over 600 catalytic converters, and the driver faces felony charges. Converter theft cases keep pressure on yards to document and verify where cats come from.
